:::{#def-iterative-method}
#### Iterative method

An **iterative method** starts from a point $\vx^{(0)}$
and computes $\vx^{(t+1)}$ from $\vx^{(t)}$ by a fixed rule, for $t = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-iterate}
#### Iterate

In an iterative method (@def-iterative-method),
the points $\vx^{(t)}$ are its **iterates**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-iterate-error}
#### Error of an iterate

For a point $\vx^*$ that an iterative method (@def-iterative-method) is meant to reach,
$\norm{\vx^{(t)} - \vx^*}$ is the **error** of the iterate $\vx^{(t)}$ (@def-iterate).

:::
